en.title: Why Singapore Airlines guarantees its pilots at least 3 horizontal hours of sleep on its longest flights
en.summary: Singapore Airlines staffs its Singapore-New York SQ24 service with four pilots and 13 cabin crew, using hidden bunks and staggered rest so pilots get at least three hours lying flat on flights of up to 19 hours and 15 minutes.
body: One of the most surprising things about a Singapore Airlines ultra-long-haul flight is not something passengers can see. A second shift of crew is asleep above their heads while the cabin carries on as normal, and the airline's pilots are guaranteed at least three hours of sleep lying fully flat. The Singapore-New York SQ24 service to John F. Kennedy International Airport carries four pilots, two captains and two first officers, plus 13 cabin crew including the purser, against a typical international flight with two pilots and eight or nine flight attendants. The cabin crew total can reach 14 on some sectors, including flights to Los Angeles. The New York route covers roughly 9,537 miles (15,349 kilometers) and can take up to 19 hours and 15 minutes in the air, far beyond what a single set of pilots may fly under duty-time rules.

The rest areas are out of sight, and not in a passenger seat. The flight attendant rest area sits toward the back of the cabin, reached by a small staircase near the fourth set of exit doors, with eight bunks behind privacy curtains. Pilots get a separate compartment above the forward business class cabin with two beds and an armchair. Pilots receive at least two rest periods during the flight, one of them lasting about four hours or more, and at least three of those hours must be spent horizontal. Cabin crew receive roughly four to five hours of rest, depending on total duty time. Every crew member works the first meal service after takeoff; once it ends, about half the cabin crew head to the bunks while the rest keep working, and the groups swap every two to three hours. In the cockpit, one pair of pilots flies while the other rests, and they swap partway through the cruise, so only two pilots sit at the controls at any one time, and everyone returns for the final service and stays seated for landing.

The aircraft itself is part of the plan. Singapore Airlines flew Singapore to New York from 2004 to 2013 with the four-engine Airbus A340-500, which burned about 25% more fuel per seat than today's aircraft, and the route was paused when fuel prices rose. It returned in 2018 on the more fuel-efficient Airbus A350-900ULR, which carries about 43,600 gallons (165,000 liters) of fuel, roughly 6,300 gallons (24,000 liters) more than a standard Airbus A350-900, and the airline took delivery of the first one on September 22, 2018. The A350-900ULR is restricted to 161 seats, 67 in business class and 94 in premium economy, with no economy or first class. According to Airbus, the A350's carbon-fiber airframe allows higher cabin humidity and a lower cabin altitude of about 5,900 feet (1,800 meters), and Singapore Airlines adds LED lighting capable of 16 million colors to simulate natural sunrise and sunset. Pilots must have 48 hours off duty before departure and receive three days of layover rest in New York, after crossing 12 time zones in one duty period.

facts.claim: Singapore Airlines' SQ24 to New York carries four pilots, two captains and two first officers, plus 13 cabin crew including the purser, and the route covers roughly 9,537 miles and can take up to 19 hours and 15 minutes.
Singapore Airlines pilots are guaranteed at least three hours of sleep lying fully flat, receiving at least two rest periods, one lasting about four hours or more.
The flight attendant rest area has eight bunks near the fourth set of exit doors, while pilots have a separate compartment above the forward business class cabin with two beds and an armchair.
Cabin crew receive roughly four to five hours of rest, work the first meal service together, then swap about every two to three hours, with all crew back for the final service and landing.

The Singapore-New York route ran from 2004 to 2013 on the Airbus A340-500, was paused when fuel prices rose, and returned in 2018 on the Airbus A350-900ULR, the first of which was delivered on September 22, 2018.
The A350-900ULR carries 161 seats, 67 in business class and 94 in premium economy, with no economy or first class, and its cabin altitude is about 5,900 feet.
Pilots must have 48 hours off duty before departure and receive three days of layover rest in New York.

zh.title: 新加坡航空超長程航班機組休息解密：飛行員至少3小時平躺睡眠
zh.summary: 新加坡航空SQ24新加坡—紐約航線配置4名飛行員與13名客艙組員，透過隱藏臥鋪與輪班休息，讓飛行員在最長19小時15分鐘的航程中至少有3小時平躺睡眠。
body: 新加坡航空超長程航班最令人意外之處，並不是乘客看得到的服務，而是機組員在乘客頭頂上方輪流休息。SQ24新加坡—紐約甘迺迪國際機場航線配置4名飛行員，包括2名機長與2名副機長，以及13名客艙組員，包含座艙長；相較之下，一般國際航班通常只有2名飛行員與8至9名客艙組員，部分前往洛杉磯的航段客艙組員可達14名。這條航線約9,537英里（15,349公里），空中飛行時間最長可達19小時15分鐘，遠超過單一組機組員在值勤時間規定下可以執飛的長度，因此必須以兩組人力輪替。

休息空間不在乘客座位，而是在視線之外。客艙組員休息區位於客艙後段，經由第四組逃生門附近的小樓梯抵達，設有8張臥鋪並以簾幕區隔；飛行員則在前方商務艙上方另有獨立空間，設有2張床與1張扶手椅。飛行員在航程中至少有2段休息時間，其中1段約4小時或更久，且至少3小時必須平躺；客艙組員則依總值勤時間不同，約可休息4至5小時。所有組員先一起完成起飛後的第一餐服務，之後約半數客艙組員前往臥鋪休息，其餘繼續值勤，每2至3小時輪換一次；駕駛艙則由一組飛行員執飛、另一組休息，在巡航中途交換，任何時刻只有2名飛行員在操控位置，所有人再一起回到崗位完成最後服務並就座降落。

這條航線的歷史也說明了人力安排為何如此重要。新加坡航空曾於2004年至2013年以4發動機空中巴士A340-500執飛新加坡—紐約航線，該機型每座燃油消耗比現今機型高約25%，後來因油價上漲而停飛；2018年改以較省油的空中巴士A350-900ULR復航，首架於2018年9月22日交付，載油量約43,600加侖（165,000公升），比標準型A350-900多約6,300加侖（24,000公升）。A350-900ULR僅設161個座位，包括67個商務艙與94個豪華經濟艙，沒有經濟艙與頭等艙；空中巴士指出，A350碳纖維機身可提高客艙濕度、將客艙高度降至約5,900英尺（1,800公尺），新加坡航空另以可呈現1,600萬色的LED燈光模擬自然日出與日落。飛行員出發前必須有48小時不值勤，並在紐約獲得3天過夜休息，以調適一次值勤就跨越12個時區的生理時鐘落差。
